voyage.name: Rathaus
voyage.content: More of a fairground than a Christmas market, this is Vienna's largest and busiest incarnation. Located on the large town square between Rathaus and Burgtheater, the Wiener Christkindlmarkt is by far the largest and probably best known Christmas market in Vienna. Large Christmas tree in front of the townhall, skating possibility, adorned trees in the park, often crowded!

voyage.name: Spittelberg
voyage.content: Probably the most delightful, though often quite packed Christmas market in Vienna, the Spittelberg market is scattered over a series of lanes lined with picturesque early 19th century Biedermeier houses (many of them former brothels, which is the reason the area was spared early 20th century urban renewal). Some of the stalls are extensions of the shops and bars of this normally rather sleepy area.

voyage.name: Maria-Theresien-Platz
voyage.content: A relatively new market between the two museums and en route to/from the MuseumsQuartier (MQ). It is easy to maneuver than some and the quality of the goods is better than most.

voyage.name: Schönbrunn
voyage.content: One of the better markets with higher quality goods and a more festive atmosphere in front of Schönbrunn palace. It is easier to spread out here and the specialties are food, handmade soaps, and candles.

voyage.name: Belvedere
voyage.content: Another addition to the city's Christmas markets, the market in front of the Belvedere palace is spacious and emphasizes the homespun.

voyage.name: Freyung
voyage.content: A fine market in the First District frequented by locals and professionals on their lunch break and downtown shoppers. Focus on handicrafts and original gifts such as hand-made Christmas decorations, mangers or objects made of natural materials. Christmas cakes and biscuits as well as hot punch and Glühwein. There are usually fewer tourists.

voyage.name: Oberlaa
voyage.content: Very Viennese cafes, really delicious bakery and well known confectionery. Also some choice of soups and mains. Several locations, mostly in Innere Stadt.

voyage.name: Aida
voyage.content: Chic but artificial design, mediocre quality, depends on location and luck. Many cafés across Vienna and Lower Austria. Their menus have a very useful graphical design indicating the precise ingredients and proportions in each type of coffee, so it's worth visiting if you are a complete beginner.

voyage.name: Wein & Co
voyage.content: A chain shop for wine lovers featuring a wine bar in every location. Shop locations include Naschmarkt, Mariahilfer Straße, near Burggarten and near Stephansplatz.

voyage.name: Why Not
voyage.content: Vienna's mainstream everyday gay disco. The crowd is varied. It is in the 1st District at Tiefer Graben 22 (Herrengasse U3). Saturdays are house music free.

voyage.name: Rosa Lilla Villa
voyage.content: A gay resource center with an excellent bar and restaurant. (Pilgramgasse U4)

voyage.name: Stephansdom
voyage.hours: Daily Mon-Sat 06:00-22:00, Sun and holidays 07:00-22:00; visits for tourists: Mon-Sat 09:00-11:30, 13:00-16:30, Sun and holidays 13:00-16:300; tour of cathedral and treasury: Mon-Sat 10:30 (English), daily 15:00 (German)
voyage.content: Yet another patchwork of architectural styles, but predominantly Gothic. None of the original construction remains, the oldest extant sections are the thirteenth century Giant Gate (Riesentor) and Towers of the Heathens (Heidentürme), both of which are Romanesque. In 1511, building in Gothic style ceased due to being out of fashion. The main altar has a Baroque panel showing St. Stephen, Christianity's first martyr.

voyage.name: South Tower
voyage.content: The 137-m-high tower, often known by its Viennese diminutive Steffl (also a nickname for the entire cathedral), was finished in 1433. 347 steps lead to the Türmerstube and to a good view.

voyage.name: North Tower
voyage.content: Steffl's intended twin, this tower was never finished. Over 50 years later, in 1579, a Renaissance spire was added to the Nordturm to make it look less like the builders had stormed off the job. This is where the Pummerin, a huge bell cast from melted-down Turkish cannons, hangs. The aborted tower has an observation deck with an amazing view of downtown Vienna.

voyage.name: Catacombs
voyage.hours: Mon-Sat 10:00-11:30, 13:30-16:30; Sun and holidays 13:30-16:30; tours depart every 15-30 min
voyage.content: Legions of bishops and Habsburg body parts are buried here (the intestines, specifically).

voyage.name: Treasury
voyage.content: Displays the most precious objects from the cathedral's treasury.

voyage.name: Roof Walk
voyage.content: For an unusual perspective of the cathedral, consider taking a 90-minute guided tour of the roof.

voyage.name: Kaisergruft
voyage.content: Underneath the Kapuzinerkirche, this mausoleum houses the tombs of generations of Habsburg royalty.

voyage.name: Jesuitenkirche
voyage.content: Has one of the most elaborate Baroque interiors in Europe.

voyage.name: Ruprechtskirche
voyage.content: Believed to be the oldest church in Vienna, although excavations around the foundations of two other churches (Stephansdom and Peterskirche) have challenged this view. Earliest mention of the church in historical records is in 1200; the current structure dates from the Romanesque period, while the interior was renovated during the Baroque era.

voyage.name: Peterskirche
voyage.content: The church is believed to date back to the Middle Ages, and excavations suggest that the foundation may be far older than previously believed. The current structure was built during the Baroque period, and restored from 1998-2004 to return the paintings to their original colouring and brightness. There are regular organ concerts at 15:00 (free).

voyage.name: Maria am Gestade
voyage.content: This gothic church was used by sailors on the Danube river. Its name refers to the former location near the river. Communion celebrations are held in German, French, and Czech.

voyage.name: Kaiserappartements
voyage.content: This trio of museums includes the Imperial Apartments (Kaiserappartements), Sisi Museum, and Imperial Silver Collection (Silberkammer). The Imperial Apartments and Sisi Museum include 22 state rooms of the residential and state apartments of Emperor Franz Joseph I and Empress Elisabeth (popularly known as Sisi) and show 19th-century imperial life. The Imperial Silver Collection displays unique items of the glittering

voyage.name: Schatzkammer
voyage.alt: Imperial Treasury; aka the Secular and Ecclesiastical Treasures
voyage.price: €6 (as a combined ticket with the Museum of Fine Arts)
voyage.content: The best part of the Hofburg and an absolute must. It contains the Habsburgs' collection of jewels, crowns, and other valuables, perhaps the best on the Continent. Second only to a tour of the Kunsthistorisches Museum, of which the Schatzkammer is a part. There are 20 rooms of priceless treasures that give a fairly accurate representation of the ceremonial Habsburg court life over the centuries.

voyage.name: New Palace
voyage.content: The newest and largest section of the Imperial Palace. It contains the Welt Museum Wien, the Papyrus Museum, and three branches of the Museum of Fine Arts.

voyage.name: Ephesos Museum
voyage.price: Admission included with ticket for Museum of Fine Arts
voyage.content: Contains classical art from Ephesus, in Asia Minor.

voyage.name: Collection of Historic Musical Instruments
voyage.price: Admission included with ticket for the Museum of Fine Arts

voyage.name: Hofjagd- und Rüstkammer
voyage.price: Admission included with ticket for the Museum of Fine Arts
voyage.content: The jewel of the New Palace is the Collection of Arms. This collection, second largest in the world, houses an immense and exhaustive representation of weaponry from past centuries.

voyage.name: Papyrusmuseum
voyage.price: €4 (adults), €3.60 (Ö1 Club and Vienna Card), €3.50 (seniors), €3 (students/military/disabled); includes admission to the Globe and Esperanto Museums (listed below with the Austrian National Library)
voyage.content: One of the largest collections of its kind in the world, it includes nearly 180,000 manuscripts spanning 3,000 years of Egyptian history. 200 items are on permanent display.

voyage.name: Weltmuseum Wien
voyage.alt: formerly the Ethnological Museum / Museum für Völkerkunde
voyage.content: This collection encompasses many thousands of artifacts from around the globe. The most famous piece in its collection however is a headdress believed to have belonged to the last Aztec emperor Moctezuma.

voyage.name: The House of Austrian History
voyage.content: The House of Austrian History is a modern museum located in the Hofburg complex that explores Austria’s history from the late 19th century to the present. Through multimedia exhibits and historical artefacts, it focuses on key events such as the end of the Habsburg monarchy, the World Wars, and the development of the modern Austrian state.

voyage.name: Austrian National Library
voyage.content: Card catalogs may be an anachronism in today’s digital world, but this library had the first one in existence, invented by the Habsburg court librarian. Unlike the printed library catalogs of the past, bound into book form, the card catalog could be rapidly updated and the library kept up-to-date. This well-ordered reader's paradise has a collection that outshines many museums, thanks to its long association with the

voyage.name: Prunksaal
voyage.content: This magnificent historic library was designed by Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach and built in 1726. As well as the spectacular room itself, you can see temporary exhibitions on various historical subjects.

voyage.name: Globenmuseum
voyage.price: €4 (adults), €3.60 (Ö1 Club or Vienna Card), €3.50 (seniors), €3 (students/military/disabled); includes admission to the Esperanto and Papyrus Museums
voyage.content: The only museum of its type in the world, this museum contains a collection of 650 globes of all types, as well as a collection of nearly 300,000 historic maps.

voyage.name: Esperantomuseum
voyage.price: €4 (adults), €3.60 (Ö1 Club or Vienna Card), €3.50 (seniors); €3 (students/military/disabled); includes admission to the Globe and Papyrus Museums
voyage.content: Founded in 1927, this museum houses a library and museum with displays illustrating the development and grammar of the modern invented language Esperanto.

voyage.name: Albertina
voyage.content: Once a palace, it is now the most popular exhibition space in Vienna, mainly for traditional modern art. The building itself is an experience as well. It is home to a valuable drawing collection, including many works of the German Renaissance painter, Dürer.

voyage.name: Herzgruft, Augustinerkirche
voyage.content: Yet another example of the gruesome divide-and-conquer burial strategy of the Habsburg dynasty. It is said that other dynasties waged countless wars to acquire new lands, but "you, happy Austria, marry". Even in death, the Habsburgs placated three different churches with the honor of caring for their remains. The best known, the Kapuzinergruft, contains their actual bodies. St Stephens holds their innards (intestines

voyage.name: Hofburgkapelle
voyage.price: Performances: seats €36/26/16, seats with no view €10; standing room only free (sold on Su at 08:30 before mass)
voyage.hours: Visiting hours: Mon Tue 10:00-14:00, Fri 11:00-13:00, closed holidays; Sun Mass: 09:15, seating no later than 09:00
voyage.content: The original chapel of the Palace, built in Gothic style 1447-1449, was made over in Baroque style. On Sundays and Catholic holidays (of which the Austrians celebrate many), the Court Musicians perform here. This group is made up of members from the Vienna Boys Choir, as well as performers from the orchestra and choir of the Vienna State Opera. Tickets can be purchased online here.

voyage.name: Spanish Riding School
voyage.hours: Visitor center: Tue-Sun 09:00-16:00, Fri 09:00-19:00 during performance days; box office (Josefsplatz): Tue-Fri 09:00-12:00
voyage.content: First mentioned in a document dated 1572, it is the only equestrian institute in the world which follows a Renaissance model of classical schooling. Eleves, or students, begin their training immediately after completion of Austrian primary education (age 15 or 16), and are expected to be both sporty and clever. The school takes its name from a Spanish breed of horse first mentioned in Roman writings. In 1562, Emperor

voyage.name: Schmetterlinghaus
voyage.content: A tropical greenhouse with an amazing collection of live butterflies, will delight both children and adults.

voyage.name: Kunsthistorisches Museum
voyage.price: €14 (adults), €11 (concessions); admission includes entry to the Ephesos Museum, Collection of Historic Musical Instruments, and Collection of Arms and Armour (see listing below under New Palace)
voyage.content: One of the world's greatest art museums and in a palace that is a work of art itself. Serious art fans may wish to devote more than a day to its treasures. There is no other word to describe the Kunst other than mind-boggling. It contains a world-class exhibit of the Habsburgs' art collection, including Raphael, Titian, Caravaggio, Bosch, and Brueghel. The museum has an excellent collection of ancient Egyptian, Greek

voyage.name: Naturhistorisches Museum
voyage.price: €10 (adults), €8 (seniors and Ö1 Club or Vienna Card), €5 (students/apprentices/military), free (disabled and children under 19)
voyage.content: This museum was erected as a mirror to its twin museum, the Museum of Fine Arts. It exhibits various minerals, meteorites, fossils, stuffed animals, and skeleton reconstructions of dinosaurs and other. It also includes an anthropological section, where you can see the beautiful Venus of Willendorf which is 25,000 years old. Most signs and explanations in the museum are only in German, and you will likely receive litt

voyage.name: Winterpalais des Prinzen Eugen
voyage.content: This Baroque palace was built as a residence for Prince Eugene of Savoy, and later used for the Court Treasury and Ministry of Finance. It now houses period furnishings and exhibits detailing the biography of the prince and the history of the palace.

voyage.name: MAK
voyage.alt: Museum für angewandte Kunst / Austrian Museum of Applied Arts
voyage.price: €12 (adults), €10 (concessions), free (children and youth under 19); 50% discount on Tu from 18:00-22:00
voyage.content: The museum has the MAK Design Shop and a study collection. The museum emphasises design and decorative arts, and has a huge furniture collection. Early 20th century, especially Vienna Secession, and modern design are very well represented, as are contemporary decorative art and design.

voyage.name: Haus der Musik
voyage.content: This is a relatively new and special museum devoted to an interactive learning experience. It covers the history of the Vienne Philharmonic Orchestra, the history of Vienna as a centre of music making (Mozart, Haydn, Beethoven, Mahler, Schubert and others are documented). In addition there are the more experimental sections of futuristic composition (the Brain Opera) and sound experiences.

voyage.name: Museum am Schottenstift
voyage.content: A nice, small picture gallery mainly of Baroque Austrian painting.

voyage.name: Gemäldegalerie der Akademie der bildenden Künste
voyage.alt: Gallery of the Academy of Fine Arts
voyage.content: A gallery owned by the Academy of Fine Arts, to which Hitler applied to before he decided to change to politics. It offers some paintings by Rubens and Bosch. Most interesting are the Renaissance and medieval exponents.

voyage.name: Museum Postsparkasse
voyage.content: SIGNA, the owner of the Post Office Savings Bank building, runs the WAGNER:WERK Museum Postsparkasse. Opened by BAWAG P.S.K. in 2005, it's in the small banking hall. The museum and the main banking hall are open to visitors. At the post office of his original design. At this museum you can see the more serious aspect of his artistic enterprise, that of public life. Also some of the original furniture and his plans.

voyage.name: Österreichisches Filmmuseum
voyage.content: A cinema for showing specially curated films and retrospective.

voyage.name: Uhrenmuseum
voyage.price: €6 (adults), €4 (seniors/students and Vienna Card), free (children and youth under 19); free the first Sunday of every month
voyage.content: A collection of 3000 clocks of all types, including a prized 18th-century astronomical clock.

voyage.name: Bank Austria Kunstforum
voyage.content: This venue hosts special exhibits of internationally-renowned artists; past exhibits have displayed work by Egon Schiele, Oskar Kokoschka, Cézanne, Picasso, and Van Gogh.

voyage.name: Phantastenmuseum
voyage.content: An unusual museum dedicated to the work of the Vienna School of Fantastic Realism (Wiener Schule des Phantastischen Realismus), highlighting works by artists Ernst Fuchs, Arik Brauer, Rudolf Hausner, Wolfgang Hutter and Fritz Janschka. An extra section of the museum displays paintings by international artists, and the first floor is devoted to rotating special exhibits.

voyage.name: Dommuseum
voyage.hours: Wed 10:00-18:00, Thu 10:00-20:00, Fri-Sun 10:00-18:00; last admission 30min before closing
voyage.content: A collection of liturgical implements, illustrated manuscripts, altarpieces, and sculptures.

voyage.name: Österreichisches Theatermuseum
voyage.content: Housed in the Baroque Lobkowitz Palace, this museum displays stage models, costumes, and props, with special temporary exhibits.

voyage.name: MUSA Museum Startgalerie Artothek
voyage.hours: Tue Wed Fri 11:00-18:00, Thu 11:00-20:00, Sat 11:00-16:00; closed Sun Mon and holidays
voyage.content: Hosts special exhibits of contemporary Austrian art.

voyage.name: Beethoven Pasqualatihaus
voyage.price: €4 (children and youth under 19), €3 (seniors/students and Vienna Card), free (children and youth under 19); free the first Sunday of every month
voyage.content: This 18th-century building is atop the Mölker Bastei, one of the only remaining sections of the old city wall. For 8 years Beethoven lived in a 4th-floor apartment in this building, where he composed his 4th-8th symphonies as well as his opera Fidelio. The museum preserves many of the composer's personal effects, and displays documents illustrating his life and work.

voyage.name: Jüdisches Museum Wien
voyage.price: €10 (adults), €8 (concessions), €5 (students), free (children under 15); includes admission to the branch on Judenplatz
voyage.hours: Sun-Fri 10:00-18:00; closed on Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur
voyage.content: A museum documenting the history of Vienna's substantial Jewish community which included Zweig, Freud, Herzl, Mahler, and Schoenberg. Three sites are available for one combined ticket: two museum sites and the main synagogue. Attached to the museum at Judenplatz are the archaeological remains of a medieval synagogue. The Stadttempel, the only historical synagogue in Vienna to have survived World War II, is accessible

voyage.name: Jüdisches Museum Judenplatz
voyage.price: €10 (adults), €8 (concessions), €5 (students), free (children under 15); includes admission to the branch on Dorotheergasse
voyage.hours: S-Thu 10:00-18:00, Fri 10:00-14:00; closed on Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur
voyage.content: A second branch of the Jewish Museum on Dorotheergasse. Underneath the Judenplatz (the Jewish Square) is an underground medieval synagogue excavation. Amazingly, the synagogue was destroyed centuries ago, but its existence was remembered by the area's inhabitants up to the 20th century.

voyage.name: Stadttempel
voyage.price: Visitation with guided tour only, arranged through the Jewish Museum
voyage.hours: Guided tours Mon-Thu 11:30, 14:00; photo ID required
voyage.content: A well preserved 19th-century synagogue, which is being used as the main city's synagogue by the current growing Viennese Jewish community.

voyage.name: Ausgrabungen Michaelerplatz
voyage.content: Archeological excavations carried out between 1989 and 1991 revealed not only the foundations of medieval buildings but also remains of the Roman canabae (civilian support settlement) of Vindobona, as Vienna was then known. The viewing area was designed by Viennese architect Hans Hollein.

voyage.name: Mozarthaus Vienna
voyage.content: This is the Viennese residence of Austria's most famous composer, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, and a branch of the Vienna Museum.

voyage.name: Neidhart Fresken
voyage.price: €4 (adults), €3 (seniors/students and Vienna Card), free (children and youth under 19); free the first Sunday of every month
voyage.content: The oldest secular wall paintings known in Vienna, in a 14th-century building. The frescoes were commissioned in 1398 and illustrate scenes from the life and poetry of the Viennese minnesinger Neidhart von Reuental.

voyage.name: Römermuseum
voyage.price: €6 (adults), €4 (seniors/students and Vienna Card), free (children and youth under 19); free the first Sunday of every month
voyage.content: This museum houses a collection of artifacts from the Roman settlement of Vindobona, as Vienna was then known. There are Roman ruins in the cellar of the museum, first discovered during construction work in 1948, and for many years only accessible to the public via a narrow staircase, before the building was transformed into a full-fledged museum 2008.

voyage.name: Römische Baureste Am Hof
voyage.content: Early Roman ruins from Vienna's earliest days as a Roman fort in the basement of the Fire Brigade Building.

voyage.name: Virgilkapelle
voyage.price: €5 (adults), €4 (seniors/students and Vienna Card), free (children and youth under 19); free the first Sunday of every month
voyage.content: A 13th-century subterranean chapel beneath the former Chapel of St Mary Magdalene (no longer standing, but outlines have been traced on the pavement directly south of Stephansdom). This chapel served as the tomb for a wealthy Viennese family and was completely forgotten until construction of the underground in 1975. A portion of it can be viewed for free from a window in the U-Bahn station.

voyage.name: Heldenplatz
voyage.content: A public space in front of the Neue Hofburg, setting to a number of important historic events, most notably of Adolf Hitler's 1938 announcement of the Austrian Anschluß. Two 19th-century equestrian statues portray Archduke Charles of Austria-Teschen and Prince Eugene of Savoy.

voyage.name: Stock im Eisen
voyage.content: The remaining midsection of a medieval nail tree (Nagelbaum). Over the centuries hundreds of nails have been hammered in both in thanksgiving and for good luck. The tree figures in a number of local legends.

voyage.name: Parlamentsgebäude
voyage.price: Tours: €5 (adults), €2.50 (seniors/students/disabled), free (children and youth under 19); Visitor Center free
voyage.hours: Visitor Center: Mon-Sat 09:30-16:30; tours only when not in use by Parliament
voyage.content: The home of the two houses of Austrian Parliament. The building was designed by Theophil von Hansen in the Neoclassical style, and constructed between 1873 and 1883. Guided tours are offered in German or English.

voyage.name: Wiener Secession
voyage.price: Beethoven Frieze + special exhibits: €8.50 (adults), €5 (seniors/students); special exhibits: €5 (adults), €4 (seniors/students); guided tours: €3
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00; guided tours Sat 15:00, Sun 11:00 and by appt
voyage.content: Architect Josef Maria Olbrich built this Jugendstil (German-style Art Nouveau) building 1897-98 as a display space for artists working in the new Secession artistic movement. It is topped by a giant, frothy golden ball, lovingly called Krauthappel by the Viennese, but the building was definitely not loved when it first opened. Notice a reactionary Viennese pattern here? The opera building too was hated at first, but

voyage.name: Wiener Rathaus
voyage.price: Free; audioguides in English/French/Italian/Spanish available with ID
voyage.hours: Tours (in German) Mon Wed Fri 13:00, no registration required
voyage.content: Designed by Friedrich von Schmidt (the architect of the Cologne Cathedral) and completed in 1883, this is the most significant neo-Gothic building in Vienna, with a 103m-high clock tower. There is a very pleasant park with two fountains in front of the building facing the Ring.

voyage.name: Ankeruhr
voyage.content: A large 4-m-diameter musical clock on a pedestrian bridge connecting two neighboring buildings. The clock was designed between 1911 and 1914 by the Judgenstil painter Franz Matsch, and features prominent figures from Viennese history, each with a Roman character. At noon all figures parade across the clock face, accompanied by music. During the Advent season, Christmas songs are played daily at 17:00 and 18:00.

voyage.name: Looshaus
voyage.content: Designed by Adolf Loos and completed in 1909, this is considered to be one of the most significant buildings of the Wiener Moderne era from 1890-1910, although initially it was fiercely criticised. Today the building is occupied by the Wiener Raiffeisenbank, but a permanent exhibit in the building has photographs and documents illustrating the building's history.

voyage.name: Universität Wien
voyage.content: The university was founded in 1365, and is the oldest university in the German-speaking area, as well as one of the largest in Europe with more than 90,000 students. It consists of 15 faculties amongst them are Law, Mathematics, Physics, Psychology and Translational Studies. The main building (Hauptgebaeude) on the Ringstraße was designed by Heinrich von Ferstel, and formally inaugurated in 1884 by the Emperor Franz

voyage.name: Ringstraße
voyage.content: The Ringstraße circles the very heart of Vienna. Built on the location of the original city walls, its size is a good indication of how much the city has expanded since medieval times, but more importantly it is the most posh area of downtown. Elegant individuals stroll down the street (there really is no other way to move when walking along the Ring) and play the fashion-do/fashion don’t game under their breath befo

voyage.name: Stadtpark
voyage.content: Court painter Joseph Selleny and garden director Rudolf Siebeck designed this kind of artificial park with several small landscapes. It opened on the 21 August 1862. It houses the golden statue of Johann Strauss, which is most frequently photographed monuments in Vienna. You can also find the monuments of Franz Schubert, Franz Lehár, Robert Stolz and Hans Makart. The park is very frequently visited by locals and tour

voyage.name: Rathauspark
voyage.content: The park is symmectric with a big square in the middle in front of the city hall. The park has on each grassy side a varied selection of woody plants a Japanese pagoda tree or umbrella tree and an old ginkgo.

voyage.name: Volksgarten
voyage.content: The park is famous for the big variation of beautiful roses and features old platanes. There is a monument for Empress Elizabeth and in the middle a neoclassical Theseus temple.

voyage.name: Burggarten
voyage.content: It has the form of an English garden, and is directly adjacent to the Hofburg. It has a statue of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. In the summertime students like to hang out in middle of the trees.

voyage.name: Wiener Staatsoper
voyage.content: Probably the most-beloved symbol of Viennese arts, and one of the first buildings to be rebuilt in the postwar era. It was built from 1861-1869 under the direction of architects Eduard van der Nüll and August von Siccardsburg for then-emperor Franz Josef I. The first performance was Don Giovanni, an opera by Austrian native Mozart, on 25 May 1869. The architecture of the opera was barely tolerated by the picky Vienne

voyage.name: Wiener Philharmoniker
voyage.content: Considered one of the world's best orchestras, subscription tickets are notoriously difficult to get with a waiting list lasting up to 13 years. Individual tickets however are available in limited numbers online from the Musikverein (where performances take place) and at the ticket office.

voyage.name: Musikverein
voyage.content: Home to the Vienna Philharmonic, and venue for a wide range of other classical music performances. Its largest hall, the Großer Musikvereinssaal (Goldener Saal) is considered to be one of the world's finest concert halls. For visitors wanting a closer look, daily 45-min guided tours are offered (entrance at Bösendorferstraße 12, adults €6, youth 12-16 €4.

voyage.name: Burgtheater
voyage.hours: Guided tour Burgtheater – Behind the Scenes: Sep-Jun Mon-Thu 15:00 (German w/English summary), Fri-Sun 15:00 (German and English); guided tour Gustav Klimt – Main Staircases and Angelika Prokopp Foyer: Sep-Jun Fri-Sun 14:00 (German w/English summary)
voyage.content: The building was completed in 1888 and is home to one of the most respected German-language theaters, as well as the second-oldest theater in Europe. Non-German speaking visitors will find the building itself worth visiting, as the foyer contains paintings by Viennese artists Gustav and Ernst Klimt, and Franz Matsch, which can be viewed with a tour.

voyage.name: Wiener Hofburg Orchester
voyage.hours: Three times a week May - mid Oct
voyage.content: Performs live. The program features the most famous waltz and operetta melodies by "the King of the Waltz", Johann Strauss, Franz Léhar and opera aries by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. It is led by conductor Gert Hofbauer, is composed of 36 musicians and six international vocal soloists from Vienna’s largest orchestral societies. On 31 Dec and 1 Jan the orchestra also performs the traditional New Year's Eve and New Year's

voyage.name: Opera Film Festival
voyage.content: Each day, weather permitting, you can watch an opera on a huge open-air screen. On another part of the square, there are plenty of food stalls (maybe a little overpriced) which offer Viennese, as well as international food. On pleasant summer evenings, the atmosphere can be quite relaxing.

voyage.name: Porgy & Bess
voyage.content: The Jazzclub features international Jazz artists. One can reserve seats in advance, which is recommended for special events. The bar offers good wine and some food too.

voyage.name: Jazzland
voyage.content: The Jazzclub plays kind of old-men Jazz in a relaxed ambiance operating since 1972.

voyage.name: Gartenbaukino
voyage.content: The biggest Viennese one projection theater cinema opened in 1960 is screening artsy production and has electronic music events. The cinema hosts Viennese premieres and can screen 70mm films too.

voyage.name: Burg Kino
voyage.content: A classic 1970s theatre which hosts international films. They regularly play The Third Man movie.

voyage.name: Casino Vienna
voyage.content: The casino is at Palais Esterhàzy, on the famous Kärtner Strasse near the Opera and is operated by state-owned Casinos Austria. In addition there are several poker casinos (e.g. Montesino) and many, many tiny slot-machine and betting places. The latter often occur in groups of three (because there is a legal limit on the number of slot machines per venue). They do not offer any glamor or flair and are best avoided by

voyage.name: Edelweiss Center
voyage.content: Austria's biggest boulder hall is in the town center. One finds tons of boulder problems to solve. They offer courses for beginners and advanced. Can get crowded on after business hours.

voyage.name: Kletterzentrum Austria
voyage.content: It has a small boulder place and some interesting structures to lead climb on.

voyage.name: Wiener Eistraum
voyage.content: Every year from late January until the beginning of March a section of the park is transformed into an outdoor ice skating rink, with music. Ice skates can be rented directly onsite, and a baggage check is available. There are also a number of food and drink booths offering warm drinks including punch, mulled wine, and tea, as well as traditional Austrian food.

voyage.name: Zentralbad Wien
voyage.content: This historic men's sauna was opened in 1889 and since then has been considered to be the premiere bathing spots of Vienna. Visitors have included Habsburg royalty and modern day celebrities.

voyage.name: Kärntner Straße
voyage.content: A major shopping street with mostly international chains.

voyage.name: Am Graben
voyage.content: An up-scale shopping promenade, with many local specialties such as Wien Porzellan. A notable landmark is the Plague Column (Pestsäule), a memorial erected in 1693 commemorating one of the last major plague epidemics which swept through Vienna in 1679.

voyage.name: Kohlmarkt
voyage.content: Perhaps the fanciest shopping area picking up from the end of the Graben jogging over to Michaelerplatz with almost exclusively high-end luxury shops and designer stores.

voyage.name: Altmann & Kühne
voyage.content: The chocolate confectioner sells for more than 100 years exquisite hand made miniature chocolate. Their boxes are beautifully designed.

voyage.name: Xocolat
voyage.content: Inside the Palais Ferstel is sold excellent handmade chocolate.

voyage.name: Augarten Porzellan
voyage.content: The finest porcelain in Europe. You can also visit their factory at the main entry to the Augarten. They are preparing a limited street-art themed line as an artistic project that is Viennese.

voyage.name: Julius Meinl am Graben
voyage.content: A legendary store. Its two floors hold many exotic as well as local wares. Even if you do not intend to buy anything, it is worth a look as there are likely things you have never heard of. The store holds just about every kind of wine you can think of, and has a great selection of pastas, chocolate, and cheese. Also has a wide selection of coffee, their own is one of the most recognised in Austria.

voyage.name: Billa
voyage.content: Its range is not as wide as that of Julius Meinl, but still better than that of a typical supermarket.

voyage.name: Dorotheum
voyage.hours: Viewing times: Mon-Fri 10:00-18:00, Sat 09:00-17:00; Sun immediately prior to auction 10:00-17:00
voyage.content: The main auction site in Austria. Exhibits all sorts of furniture, art, jewelry, etc. Highly recommended. There are several locations throughout the city, the main one being at Dorotheergasse 17 in the city centre. The surrounding streets in this area offer a great many antique shops, where quality and prices tend both to be very high.

voyage.name: A. E. Köchert
voyage.content: Jakob Heinrich Köchert founded the jewellery in 1814 in collaboration with the artistic French goldsmith Emanuel Pioté. The high end jewellery is dedicated to the fine art of goldsmithing and gemstone.

voyage.name: Kniže & Comp.
voyage.content: The famous Viennese tailor's house provides the finest bespoke suits since 1858. If you're looking for traditional apparel like a smoking jacket, this is the place to have it custom tailored. It also sells various gentleman accessories like cologne. Parts of the interior like the Dodekaeder lamps were designed by Adolf Loos. It has a saddle seat to fit elegant ridding clothing.

voyage.name: Mühlbauer Manufaktur
voyage.content: Producing hats since 1903, carefully manufacted in Vienna and worn worldwide by artists or anyone who fancies beautiful hats.

voyage.name: L. Bösendorfer Piano Showroom
voyage.content: Pianists may want to visit the Bösendorfer showroom. All pianos are built by hand in nearby Wiener Neustadt.

voyage.name: Musikhaus Doblinger
voyage.content: Has sold sheet music in Vienna since 1817 and is internationally renowned.

voyage.name: Morawa
voyage.content: Probably the largest bookstore in Vienna, with a large travel section (some books in English) and a broad range of international magazines. A good selection of English-language books is shelved on the top floor.

voyage.name: Schwanda
voyage.content: One of the larger mountaineering shops of Vienna sells various outdoor gear including climbing shoes and tents.

voyage.name: Taste it
voyage.content: The place sells classy high-end Italian espresso machines and self-imported coffee from small Italian roasteries.

voyage.name: Espresso Perfetto Wien GmbH
voyage.content: Coffee machines and coffee beans.

voyage.name: Esterházykeller
voyage.content: Atmospheric old (since 1683) cellar restaurant serving good, cheap, wine, beer, and simple traditional food. Prices budget to moderate. A good place to go if you just want a drink and some grub, but still want to enjoy some local colour.

voyage.name: Schachtelwirt
voyage.content: Good schnitzel, potatoes and pork. The food is very good, different from what you can eat in typical Austrian restaurants. Cool atmosphere.

voyage.name: Chattanooga
voyage.content: Fast food versions of local food. Not bad if you are on a budget and do not have much time to spare.

voyage.name: Gasthaus zum Holunderstrauch
voyage.content: Recommendation if you are looking for home-style, local food. The atmosphere is cozy. The service provides competent and friendly advice.

voyage.name: Maschu Maschu
voyage.content: Good for veggies and meat eaters alike. Maschu Maschu is an Israeli fast food joint that serves some of the best falafel in the world. A healthy and gut-busting falafel and beer should leave you set up for the day (they also serve a wide range of other Middle Eastern meals).

voyage.name: Trzesniewski
voyage.content: The snack bar sells small breads (Brötchen) with specific spread (Aufstrich). One has many choices including vegetarian. The place is very full at lunch time, but the queue advances quickly. They only use organic eggs. The smallest possible beer (Pfiff) is available, otherwise they sell excellent fruit juices too. One eats either standing next to a table or on the go.

voyage.name: Fladerei Salzgries
voyage.content: Really nice flat bread. Open until late. Plenty of choice for vegetarians too.

voyage.name: Leberkas-Pepi
voyage.content: Authentic local fast food. Very good meatloaf and other convenient Vienna traditional light meals.

voyage.name: Würstelstand zum Hohen Markt
voyage.content: Legendary stall at Hoher Markt. As always great sausages.

voyage.name: Wiener Würstl
voyage.content: Great sausage. The seller can explain everything about all types of sausages.

voyage.name: Würstelstand am Schottentor
voyage.content: A lovely spot for street meat. Good flavors and great/friendly service.

voyage.name: Palmenhaus
voyage.content: Good value for money, great ambience with imperial decor. Large mains served with a bowl of salad included. Very high ceilings, full of air and palms. Friendly staff speaks fluent English. Children-safe wide couches. Consider seating at elevated Mezzanine (reservation recommended) which has a special view over park. On warm days one can sit outside.

voyage.name: Inigo
voyage.price: Mains around €10, average dinner with a glass of wine €20 (June 2016)
voyage.content: Modern and diverse cuisine, not crowded but most visitors are local. Charming modern interior instead of imperial chic. Overall, a rare combination of features. Menu has equal parts for vegetarians and carnivores. Friendly to families with toddlers. Staff speaks only basic English. Great bulghur here.

voyage.name: Brezl-Gwölb
voyage.content: A very nice restaurant with a cellar dating back to the 17th century. The furniture consists of parts from three centuries. A place that deserves the label gemütlich. They play classical music and serve some really unique dishes.

voyage.name: Figlmüller
voyage.content: Famous for Wienerschnitzel. They claim to have the biggest schnitzel in the world. If you are not really hungry, one may easily be enough for two people (just ask for a second plate). Traditionally, you would want a potato salad with that.

voyage.name: Le Bol
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri from 08:00, Sat Sun and holidays from 10:00
voyage.content: Fine French Provencal-style fare with a communal table at the center, goat cheese salad is highly recommended (6.90 EUR).

voyage.name: Reinthaler Gasthaus
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 09:00-23:00, kitchen 11:30-22:00; closed Sat Sun and holidays
voyage.content: One of the better traditional Beisl restaurants, with old fashioned food priced below comparable places. Daily specials usually include a couple of vegetarian options.

voyage.name: Zum Leupold
voyage.content: A bourgeois Viennese restaurant offering good seasonal local food. In summertime you can sit outdoors.

voyage.name: Ristorante Rossini
voyage.content: An Italian place serving good mostly authentic Italian food.

voyage.name: Vietthao
voyage.content: The Vietnamese restaurant offers lots of vegetarian choices. Their vegetables are well prepared using good herbs combinations.

voyage.name: Akakiko
voyage.content: Part of a local chain. Informal and popular place serving generic but reasonably priced Japanese and Korean dishes. The menu has a vegetarian section. Quick service by efficient waiters.

voyage.name: Artner am Franziskanerplatz
voyage.content: Belongs to a famous winery Artner. It offers creative, fresh fare that tends to be on the lighter side than most Austrian cuisine. Excellent wine cellar, reservations recommended.

voyage.name: Bauer
voyage.content: The restaurant since 25 years serves excellent food with Viennese charme and a big wine choice. It has one Michelin star.

voyage.name: Bristol Lounge
voyage.alt: Restaurant Bristol - Das Restaurant bei der Oper
voyage.content: The big lunch room in the Hotel Bristol reopened with the original art déco chandeliers and decorated ceiling. The restaurant may serve as elegant after Opera dinner.

voyage.name: Daihachi
voyage.content: Sushi bar popular with business travellers. Serves fresh and tasty fish that comes at a high price.

voyage.name: Fabios
voyage.content: Italian fish restaurant combined with bar/lounge for Vienna's glitterati. Quality is excellent.

voyage.name: Palais Coburg
voyage.content: The gourmet restaurant is handled by 2 Michelin-starred chef Silvio Nickol. It offers a 5-, 7- or 9-course menu. The seasonal wine card is exquisite.

voyage.name: Plachutta
voyage.content: A very nice restaurant that specialises in beef (claimed to be only local and from trusted farmers) and has some flavour of traditional Austrian cuisine. Try the Tafelspitz, it comes in a copper pan and still is in the soup it was cooked (the soup alone is worth a trip to Vienna). Alternatively, try the Backhendl. The chef claims that they prepare more than 100 kg of beef each day. Probably three to five waiters will

voyage.name: Procacci
voyage.content: Excellent northern Italian fare with a range of fine specialties. Slightly small portions but an extensive wine list to drown this particular sorrow in. Reservations recommended.

voyage.name: TIAN Restaurant
voyage.content: Star chef Paul Ivić from Tyrol leads one of only two vegetarian Michelin-starred restaurants in Europe, with an excellent wine selection. Occasionally he also offers workshops. Reservations can be made online or by phone.

voyage.name: Unkai
voyage.content: The Japanese cook Hiroshi Sakai once governed this place that serves authentic Japanese food. One dines on the top floor of a splendid Viennese palace, that is nowadays the Grand Hotel. It has an excellent choice of special wines. The restaurant is awarded with Gault-Millau caps.

voyage.name: Vestibül
voyage.content: Viennese bourgeois restaurant cooked by Christian Domschitz.

voyage.name: Weinbotschaft
voyage.content: The restaurant offers a menu with freshly cooked organic ingredients – from the classic Wiener Schnitzel to Chocolate-Almond-Cake without flour and Bio-Fruit-Ice-Cream.

voyage.name: Eissalon am Schwedenplatz
voyage.content: Maybe the most popular place. You can choose from a lot of different flavors, but it's always crowded and you often have to stand in a queue for a few minutes.

voyage.name: Eissalon am Tuchlauben (Perizzolo)
voyage.content: Another excellent and popular ice cream parlour. Ask for the Special Nougat ice cream.

voyage.name: Eis-Greissler
voyage.content: A small ice parlour that has been overrun by customers since its opening in 2011. They sell excellent organic ice cream, made from milk of their own organic milk farm and without artificial flavours. It is worth the wait in the queue.

voyage.name: Ferrari Gelato
voyage.content: The Italian ice cream shop produces on the spot their own with exquisite ingredients like piemontese hazelnuts, caramelised pine nuts or fresh fruits.

voyage.name: Zanoni & Zanoni Gelateria
voyage.content: In the same district as Eissalon. Popular with Viennese and tourists for its huge €2 cones to go.

voyage.name: Café Bräunerhof
voyage.content: Thomas Bernhard used to come here daily as do many other Viennese literate. It exists since more than 35 years. Happily expect Viennese grumpy senior waiters.

voyage.name: Café Central
voyage.content: One of the most famous Vienna coffee houses, which opened in 1876, has been authentically restored. Beautiful premises inside the Palais Ferstel, it is too touristy and a bit more expensive for having a meal, but can be worth it for a cup of coffee. There is an occasional pianist that is delightful to hear.

voyage.name: Café Diglas
voyage.content: Famous traditional coffeehouse, and equally good place for having a meal. They opened a second branch on Fleischmarkt.

voyage.name: Café Frauenhuber
voyage.content: This traditional café already existed at the times of Mozart and Beethoven. It serves Viennese food.

voyage.name: Café Gerstner
voyage.content: A very traditional Viennese café, hence visitors take their time to enjoy the lovely cakes.

voyage.name: Café Hawelka
voyage.content: One of the most famous intellectual cafes in Vienna. Established in 1939. Surprisingly cheap for its location and its fame and can get quite cozy. Josephine Hawelka (former owner, deceased 2005) was proud of the marriages she caused by placing random people together at tables. Try the Buchteln.

voyage.name: Café Landtmann
voyage.price: Breakfast sets €7-12.50, menu of the day around €11, starters €8-14, soup €4-8, schnitzel €20, coffee €4
voyage.hours: 07:30-24:00; all menus until 11:30, except Franz Landtmann served until 15:00
voyage.content: Old café, cozy and romantic. Used to be frequented by Sigmund Freud. Delicious food and desserts.

voyage.name: Café Museum
voyage.content: This cafe was designed by famous architect Adolf Loos, however the interior has been entirely refitted (most recently from 2010). Serves food, coffee, teas, and other drinks. Casual, quiet atmosphere.

voyage.name: Café Prückel
voyage.hours: Daily 08:00-22:00; live music Mon Wed Fri 19:00-22:00; closed 24-26 Dec
voyage.content: Established in 1903. Quite the hang-out in the evening, during the day this cafe is a bit more laissez-faire.

voyage.name: Café Sacher Wien
voyage.content: The Café Sacher, directly in front of the Opera House, of course serves the famous cake Sacher Torte.

voyage.name: Sacher Eck
voyage.content: The Sacher bar next to their shop is on the Corner of Kärtner Strasse and is a bit less formal than the traditional café. Still on rush hours expect some waiting time to get seated in order to be able to order the "Sacher Torte".

voyage.name: Cafe Schwarzenberg
voyage.content: Beautiful traditional Viennese café with view on the Schwarzenbergplatz and the Ring avenue. It has fine pastries and coffee choices.

voyage.name: Café Tirolerhof
voyage.content: Quaint, traditional café with art deco accents. Established in 1900.

voyage.name: Conditorei Sluka
voyage.content: A very traditional small Viennese café, opened at the end of the 19th century by Josef and Josefine Sluka, serves excellent pastries and bread. To the breakfast you can order oeuf poché. The choice on the menu is adjusted according season. Free Wi-Fi is available and in summer time you can sit outside.

voyage.name: Demel
voyage.content: Café and confectionary shop. Good pastries are ubiquitous in Vienna, but Demel is considered by many to have the best of all and indeed was once the pastry caterer to the Imperial household. As a result of this it is usually jammed with tourists, though their amusing marzipan display window can be admired even from the street. Outdoor seating in warm weather, but the inside is more atmospheric.

voyage.name: Kleines Café
voyage.content: As the name suggests, this café is rather small. It was created by architect Hermann Czech during the 1970s for notable Austrian actor Hanno Pöschl, who still owns it. It is a popular meeting place for artists and actors (or would-be variants) and enjoys an excellent location in a quiet square inside the city. The few seats are often occupied but hang around and they are vacated regularly. Seating on the square in fi

voyage.name: Vollpension
voyage.content: Intergenerational café run as a social business: the cakes are baked by senior citizens to their own family recipes and served in a vintage living-room setting. Vegetarian lunch menu on weekdays, shaded outdoor seating in summer, wheelchair accessible. Reservations online.

voyage.name: 1516 Brewing Company
voyage.content: A brewery and a bar with quality beers. The food menu includes Viennese classics as well as standard American bar food like burgers, chicken wings, and BBQ ribs. 1516 particularly caters to American and British expats, although it's also popular among Viennese locals.

voyage.name: Alt Wien
voyage.content: This cafe/restaurant/bar is on a very medieval-looking lane in the central district and is a time warp of another kind: its folky-bohemian atmosphere could convince you that you're in North Beach or Greenwich Village, circa 1967. Liveliest late.

voyage.name: Bonbonniere Tagesbar
voyage.content: Special establishment where the time stood still.

voyage.name: Dino's
voyage.content: The bar serves classical cocktails.

voyage.name: Flex
voyage.content: You have not been to Vienna if you have not been to the Flex, particularly if you are younger than thirty. The meeting point of the off-mainstream, bohemian, artsy people. During the summer nights when it is warm, there are always a lot of people sitting on benches outside the club. It's easy to socialise and make new friends. Inside the club you can enjoy bands and DJs. At the bar you can ask for free soda water.

voyage.name: Loos American Bar
voyage.alt: Loos Bar, Kärntner Bar, American Bar
voyage.content: Built in 1908, this small bar was designed by Adolf Loos and inspired by his stay in the US from 1893-1896, and will delight fans of Art Deco. Famous for its architecture and interior decoration, it is a time warp of Vienna from 1908 when it opened. Drinks are expensive, but very good and the price is worth the experience. This is a quiet, sophisticated bar, where boisterous behavior or very casual dress will not be

voyage.name: Roberto
voyage.content: The former chief bar keeper of the Loos Bar, Roberto Pavlovic opened a new American bar. It serves aperitifs 16:00–18:00, and 16:00–20:00 Champagne price is reduced. 200 cocktails to choose from.

voyage.name: Schrittesser
voyage.content: The place is specialised on Carinthian drinks and food. Speck in all kinds is served. Carinthian noodles and Schnaps are recommended too. The bar is hidden behind the Viennese university.

voyage.name: Bermuda Triangle
voyage.content: A night-life area popular for young people as the alcoholic beverages are cheap.

voyage.name: Club Passage
voyage.content: An upscale club.

voyage.name: Volksgarten Clubdiskothek
voyage.content: Up-market.

voyage.name: Badeschiff
voyage.price: Bar/restaurant: daily 10:00-01:00; pool: adults €5, children under 12 €2.50
voyage.content: An orange boat. All sorts of events and parties go on here, and in summer you can take a dip in the outdoor pool-barge during the day. There is a lower level that is the main club at big parties and a more comfortable lounge upstairs.

voyage.name: Pension Dr. Geissler
voyage.content: A family-run guest house for budget travellers with free Wifi internet and breakfast.

voyage.name: Pension Aviano
voyage.content: Small pension. Good breakfast, very friendly to families with toddler (except a small staircase prior to elevator). Free grog for guests in the afternoon. Free excellent wifi in all rooms. Helpful reception most of the time, also in finding a right place to eat.

voyage.name: Residenz Hotel Pension
voyage.content: Three-star hotel, pets permitted, free wi-fi, non-smoking.

voyage.name: Hotel Mercure Wien Zentrum
voyage.content: Modern chain hotel on a quiet cul-de-sac in the city centre. Convenient to U-Bahn, trams, and airport coaches. Rate includes wireless Internet access.

voyage.name: Hollmann Beletage
voyage.content: Boutique hotel. Only 25 rooms, contemporary design, gourmet breakfast.

voyage.name: Hotel Imperial
voyage.content: Built in 1863 as a Viennese residence for the German Prince of Württemberg in neo-Renaissance style. In total imperial style and impeccable service.

voyage.name: Hotel Palais Coburg
voyage.content: A converted historic building that now has an outstanding restaurant (perfect wine list) and spa. Beside some rooms mostly suites and impeccable service.

voyage.name: Hotel Sacher
voyage.content: This hotel is best known as the place where Sachertorte (cake) was invented. The elegant drawing room is a popular place to gather after a performance at the opera. The food is pricey but definitely worth the money. The rooms offer old style luxury with heavy carpets.

voyage.name: Le Méridien Vienna
voyage.content: Opened in late 2003 and is done in a very modern, artsy Art + Tech design. All rooms have flat screen TVs and massage showers. Features a breakfast buffet and bar.

voyage.name: Park Hyatt Vienna
voyage.content: This hotel is in a bank headquarter building in the very centre of Vienna that is more than 100 years old. It has 143 guestrooms including 35 suites. It hosts an extensive fitness centre and guests can swim in the 15-m pool in the former vault of the bank.

voyage.name: The Ring Hotel
voyage.content: Five-star boutique hotel. Has an unexpected interior, which mixes the traditional with the modern. Many of the building's historic details have been preserved to ensure the hotel remains all of its historic charm.

voyage.name: Vienna Marriott Hotel
voyage.content: 313 rooms and suites, an indoor pool and health club, business center and shops. The restaurants and bars are popular gathering places.

voyage.name: Schloß Belvedere
voyage.price: Combination ticket for Upper and Lower Palaces: €19 (adults), €15.50 (seniors/students), free (under 18)
voyage.content: Intended as a summer residence for Prince Eugene of Savoy, was outside the city walls. Its two palace segments, the Upper and Lower Belvedere, later became the permanent home of the Austrian Gallery.

voyage.name: Österreichische Galerie Belvedere
voyage.content: Contains recent Austrian and international art from the past two centuries. Viennese art from the early 20th century is well-represented in the permanent collection Vienna around 1900 and the Art of the Classical Modern, and includes masterpieces from Gustav Klimt, Oskar Kokoschka, and Egon Schiele, as well as earlier works by the Biedermeier painter Ferdinand Georg Waldmüller.

voyage.name: Unteres Belvedere
voyage.content: The Lower Belvedere and Orangery house temporary exhibits. The Baroque state rooms including the Marble Gallery, Golden Room, and Grotesque Hall are open for normal visiting.

voyage.name: Prunkstall
voyage.content: The former stables now house a permanent collection of medieval religious art and a collection of medieval tapestries.

voyage.name: 21er Haus
voyage.alt: Museum für zeitgenössische Kunst / Museum of Contemporary Art
voyage.hours: Wed Thu 11:00-21:00, Fri-Sun 11:00-18:00; open on holidays
voyage.content: Has a permanent exhibit of works by the Austrian sculptor/architect Fritz Wotruba, and hosts rotating exhibits of international contemporary art.

voyage.name: KunstHausWien
voyage.content: Even an avowed hater of modern art can appreciate this. This is Hundertwasser's (born Friedrich Stowasser in 1928) major contribution to the Viennese art world. In a time when artists often try to shock the public or merely impress other members of the rarefied gallery subculture, Hundertwasser's KunstHausWien would be a bastion against the dictatorship of the straight line, the ruler and T-square, a bridgehead again

voyage.name: Heeresgeschichtliches Museum
voyage.content: A huge museum featuring weapons and military maps from different periods. You can also see the open-top car in which Archduke Franz Ferdinand, the last Austrian prince, was shot in Sarajevo. His death triggered World War I and the eventual downfall of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. In the same room as this is the visibly blood-stained jacket he was wearing at the time of his assassination.

voyage.name: Fälschermuseum
voyage.content: Unique museum devoted to art forgery. Houses a large collection of counterfeited paintings, many from highly-skilled, infamous forgers. Includes several pages of the infamous fake Hitler diaries which fooled numerous experts in the early 1980s.

voyage.name: Remise - Verkehrsmuseum der Wiener Linien
voyage.alt: Museum of public transport (formerly known as Straßenbahnmuseum / Streetcar Museum)
voyage.content: This museum in a former depot houses a comprehensive collection of vintage vehicles explaining the history of Viennese public transport. The exhibits include horse-drawn streetcars from 1868, a steam tram set from 1885, many electric streetcars from the 1910s until the recent past, and buses from 1949-1978, including the infamous "Reichsbrücken-Bus" which fell into the Danube but was recovered and repaired to run for

voyage.name: Hundertwasserhaus
voyage.content: Interesting apartment/office complex, designed by the Austrian architect/painter Hundertwasser. Remember that most of it is still in use as housing or offices and respect the residents' privacy. The nearby KunstHausWien (see above) is a Hundertwasser building you can freely explore.

voyage.name: Schwarzenbergplatz
voyage.content: The Schwarzenberg place is a big square in inner Vienna. It is faced by many palaces amongst them the Palais Schwarzenberg, the hosue of industry, the French embassy and others.The square runs next to the RIng.

voyage.name: Heldendenkmal der Roten Armee
voyage.content: An imposing Soviet-style monument near Karlsplatz commemorates the Soviet victory in Vienna over the Nazi army.

voyage.name: Arnold Schönberg Center
voyage.price: €5 (adults), €3 (seniors/students), free (children under 12), 10% reduction for Vienna Card
voyage.content: This building houses an archive of the works of the Viennese composer, with a permanent exhibit relating to his work and music and a gallery of his paintings.

voyage.name: Sankt Marxer Friedhof
voyage.content: This historic cemetery was in use from 1784 until 1874. Mozart was buried here in an unmarked pauper's grave in 1791; the tombstone dates from a later period, after his grave was tentatively identified. The Bezirksmuseum Landstraße offers regular guided tours of the cemetery (in German).

voyage.name: Botanischer Garten
voyage.hours: Hours vary by season and weather, generally 10:00-15:00/18:00
voyage.content: Established in 1754 by Empress Maria Theresia as a garden for medicinal plants and granted to the University of Vienna, which has maintained it since. The gardens contain a number of rare plants, including alpine specimens.

voyage.name: Konzerthaus
voyage.hours: Box office: Mon-Fri 09:00-19:45, Sat 09:00-13:00; Sat Sun holidays: 45 min prior to performance
voyage.content: Built between 1911 and 1913, the Konzerthaus is the homebase for the Vienna Symphony (Wiener Symphoniker), the Vienna Chamber Orchestra (Wiener Kammerorchester), the Wiener Singakademie and the Klangforum Wien.

voyage.name: Arena
voyage.content: The arena is one of the biggest concert and alternative culture places. The slaughterhouse got squatted in 1976 and operates since as culture center. FM4 hosts here its annual birthday party. The programme lists the performing artists. The open air arena can host 3000 peoples.

voyage.name: Akademietheater
voyage.content: The Akademietheater is the smaller of two performance halls of the Burgtheater ensemble. It was built between 1911 and 1913 by the architects Fellner und Hellmer and Ludwig Baumann.

voyage.name: Ice skating
voyage.content: At the Wiener Eislaufverein in winter time one can skate on a big 6000 m² square.

voyage.name: Landstraßer Haupstraße
voyage.content: A relatively upper middle-class neighbourhood shopping street, with a wide variety of business from pubs and clubs to organic shops to second-hand stores. The Rochus Market, Rochusmarkt, and a shopping arcade are located along this street as well.

voyage.name: Mocca Brasil
voyage.content: The coffee shop also sells and repairs coffee machines. The main reason to come here is to purchase good coffee beans. They are one of the very few places in Vienna which even sells excellent green beans, and their roastery offers many choices.

voyage.name: wakeup
voyage.content: Mario Sciurti sells Italian Espresso-machines. The shop serves a short espresso (Ristretto).

voyage.name: Vegetasia
voyage.content: Chain of vegetarian restaurants. Serves a huge variety of Taiwanese Buddhist vegetarian food. Most of it vegan, many meat imitations. Non-smoking.

voyage.name: Rochusmarkt
voyage.content: Typical Viennese outdoor market with fresh produce as well as stalls selling baked goods and other prepared food.

voyage.name: Amon
voyage.content: The restaurant serves seasonal Viennese food typically of course plates with large quantities. The cellar is a vinothek with a good selection of Austrian wines.

voyage.name: Benkei
voyage.content: Favorite place from nearby Japanese embassy. The place has a bit dated interior.

voyage.name: El Fontroussi
voyage.content: The Belgium restaurant in this renovated tavern offers seafood with refined sauces. Daily lunch menu.

voyage.name: Marx Restauration
voyage.content: The restaurant inside an old butchery serves modern Viennese food. Free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: No. 27
voyage.content: The Chinese restaurant is best visited with several persons to be able to taste their different plates.

voyage.name: O'Connor's Old Oak
voyage.content: Gareth "Gaz" Smith is cooking here daily, hence this Irish pub may serve the best Irish food in Vienna (not only legendary fish and chips).

voyage.name: Pho & Saigon Market NR
voyage.content: A Vietnamese restaurant next to the shop has small delicate choices. The cellar has one table tennis.

voyage.name: Sri Thai Imbiss
voyage.content: The small cellar place cooks Thai food (green curry,..) on the spicy side of life.

voyage.name: Taverna Lefteris
voyage.content: The Cretan (not Greek) restaurant changes its menu daily.

voyage.name: Rochus
voyage.content: Contemporary Viennese and European cuisine. Vegan options available. Extensive wine and cocktail list.

voyage.name: al Italiana
voyage.content: Traditional Italian pizzeria and trattoria. Friendly service, extensive menu, good wine list. Popular with locals.

voyage.name: Meierei im Stadtpark
voyage.content: The very posh restaurant offers 120 different cheese varieties combined with freshly baked Viennese bread. This is the "bistro" of the Steiereck, but still extremely classy.

voyage.name: Steirereck im Stadtpark
voyage.content: The most renowned Austrian restaurant in middle of the beautiful Stadtpark is defintely worth a visit. Heinz Reitbauer is cooking with exotic or mostly forgotten natural herbs. Much of the menu features modernistic presentations of traditional Central European meats such as venison, carp, and crayfish. Adi Schmid is the leading Sommelier. Reservation in advance is definitely needed.

voyage.name: That’s Amore
voyage.content: Italian cooks use well chosen products for their pizzas.

voyage.name: Cafe Menta
voyage.content: Designed by Robin Molenaar and Yvonne Krisch with Rainer seats and an industrial bar, the café has a cool look plus interesting vegetarian options.

voyage.name: Intermezzo Bar
voyage.content: Incredible lustre above the bar from the 1960s.

voyage.name: Salm Bräu
voyage.content: The brewery has a Viennese kitchen, but people mostly come for the good beer.

voyage.name: Strandbar Hermann
voyage.content: The outdoor bar serves daily happy hour cocktails during 18:00-19:00. As the name tells it is a bar on sand next to the Danube canal near the Urania.

voyage.name: Vienna Sporthotel
voyage.content: Spa and tennis possibilities.

voyage.name: Hotel Am Konzerthaus - MGallery Collection
voyage.content: The rooms are nice and smallish, but still stylish.

voyage.name: Best Western Plus Amedia Hotel Wien
voyage.content: Rather boring outside and inside (although with liberal use of red), the hotel is easy to miss at the far end of Landstrasser Hauptstrasse. Amedia marks high on comfort, cleaniness and service, which is a combination rarely found in Viennese hotels.

voyage.name: Lindner Hotel Am Belvedere
voyage.content: Surprisingly tasteful, with large rooms, oversized beds and very reasonable pricing - and next to the Belvedere gardens indeed. You can get airline miles with many frequent flier programmes by staying at Lindner hotels.

voyage.name: Mercure Grand Hotel Biedermeier Wien
voyage.content: More Biedermeier than grand, this Mercure is a very typical representative of Viennese hotels, with questionable colours and patterns, all wrapped in a vaguely historic setting. That said, the unusually large rooms (esp. Privilege) make it an option worth considering. Many rooms face the narrow internal courtyard, i.e. another room's windows within a short distance.

voyage.name: NH Wien Belvedere
voyage.content: The NH corporate unformization did not quite make it to this hotel, but you can expect reasonable standards - and a simpler format of the typical Viennese hotel. Next door to the Lindner, the NH is indeed close to the Belvedere

voyage.name: Austria Trend Hotel Savoyen
voyage.content: The hotel offers spacious and modern rooms including great breakfast.

voyage.name: Hilton Vienna
voyage.content: Home to Vienna’s premier conference centre. Features meeting space for 2-1,800 and provides a business service centre.

voyage.name: Imperial Riding School Renaissance Vienna
voyage.content: This Renaissance is one of the Marriott properties scattered across Vienna, located in a renovated historic building of the former Imperial Riding School - not to be confused with the Spanish Riding School, which is far away from it. With an impressive interior and rooms appointed with decorations referencing the equine history, it surely does impress.

voyage.name: Intercontinental Wien
voyage.content: See above for the bar.

voyage.name: Spiess & Spiess
voyage.content: Classy older hotel on a quiet side street, tastefully renovated and modernized. Good-quality breakfast buffet included in the price.

voyage.name: Wien Museum Karlsplatz
voyage.content: A museum documenting Vienna's history. It is split into several branches with its main branch at Karlsplatz.

voyage.name: Dritte Mann Museum
voyage.content: This is a private museum dedicated to the cult film The Third Man, which was shot in Vienna and released in 1949. This film is often played at the Burgkino.

voyage.name: Generali Foundation
voyage.price: €6 (adults), €3 (concessions, and Th after 18:00), free (students on T)
voyage.hours: Exhibits: Tue-Sun 11:00-18:00, Thu 11:00-20:00, public holidays 11:00-18:00; archives/library Wed Thu 12:00-18:00, or by appt
voyage.content: This private foundation houses large collection of contemporary art, with a special focus on photograph, film, video, and installation pieces. The archives and library are also open to the public.

voyage.name: Schubert Sterbewohnung
voyage.price: €5 (adults), €4 (seniors/students/Vienna Card), free (children and youth under 19), free the first Su of every month
voyage.content: The composer Franz Schubert died here in 1828. The small museum displays documents relating to the composer's life and work.

voyage.name: Karlskirche
voyage.content: Largest Baroque church north of the Alps, designed by the famous architect Bernhard Fischer von Erlach. Frescos done by Michael Rottmayr and paintings from the Italian Baroque painters Sebastiano Ricci and Giuseppe Antonio Pellegrini, and the Austrian painter Daniel Gran.

voyage.name: Karlsplatz Stadtbahn Pavilion
voyage.content: An original entrance building for the Wiener Stadtbahn railway station at Karlsplatz (now U-Bahn line U4), designed by Otto Wagner. It is a good example of functional turn of the century architecture – ornate, yet useful. Wagner was one of the most influential architects in Vienna and his style was widely copied. No longer used to access the station, the building now houses a small exhibition on Wagner and the Vienne

voyage.name: Paulanerkirche
voyage.content: Built in the 17th century, the current appearance of the church is largely Baroque.

voyage.name: Palais Schönburg
voyage.content: The small Baroque garden palace is one of the earlier works of Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt. It was modified in the 19th century, and these days used as an event location.

voyage.name: Schikaneder Kino
voyage.content: The cinema features art and non mainstream films. It also participates to smaller film festivals.

voyage.name: Freie Bühne Wieden
voyage.content: The place opened in 1976 and has first releases.

voyage.name: Moki Mobiles Kindertheater
voyage.content: A theatre with plays for kids.

voyage.name: Theater Akzent
voyage.price: Tickets sold at Argentinierstraße 37, M-F 13:00-18:00, Sa 14:00-18:00, closed Jul and Aug
voyage.content: It has three different play stages: Theater Akzent, Podium im Akzent and Studio im Akzent.

voyage.name: Wiener Wortstätten
voyage.content: Founded in 2005 by Hans Escher and Bernhard Studlar, and features intercultural theatre.

voyage.name: Schleifmühlgasse
voyage.content: This little cobbled lane is home to many excellent contemporary art galleries, as well as some fine restaurants.

voyage.name: Wiedner Hauptstraße
voyage.content: A quiet shopping street with mostly small business selling oddities like stamps and a few tranquil cafes and bars.

voyage.name: Favoritenstraße
voyage.content: A neighborhood street with regular shops like pharmacies and groceries, but a very lively one and a good example of where most Viennese do their everyday business.

voyage.name: Edelgreisslerei Opocensky
voyage.content: The shop sells excellent Austrian food and wines.

voyage.name: Hang Loose Surf Shop
voyage.content: The surf shop sells wind surfing and kite equipment during spring/summer. In winter time one finds here a big choice of snowboards or free skis. The owner and the seller are sports-man themselves and hence can provide excellent advises.

voyage.name: Kaffeerösterei Alt Wien
voyage.content: The coffee roastery sells special blends from every major global coffee-producing region, including such excellent specialty coffees as organic Brazilian.

voyage.name: Kaffeefabrik
voyage.content: Tobias Radinger sells directly imported, fresh-roasted coffees.

voyage.name: Maftei shoemaker
voyage.content: The Maftei family is crafting shoes since 1925. Every shoe is handmade and unique. Alexandru Maftei uses and selects leather from the best tannieres. The double stitched seam is crafted for the chosen bespoke shoe.

voyage.name: Paninoteca
voyage.content: Small delicious little Italian sandwiches for takeaway. They offer free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Salon Wichtig
voyage.content: Dubbed the best curry in town, it has vegetarian options and the food is freshly cooked. Most people choose takeaway; one can sit nearby in front of Karlskirche.

voyage.name: Aromat
voyage.content: This place has an excellent different dinner menu with vegetarian option every week. It has the best crêpes in Vienna, but is unfortunately a smokers restaurant. Reservations are strongly recommended.

voyage.name: Babette's
voyage.content: The small kitchen-bookstore serves an excellent lunch menu, with usually one vegetarian choice. The tables/bar can accommodate only a small number of people. Patrons can watch the food preparation and learn cooking tips.

voyage.name: Chang
voyage.content: Next to the upscale restaurant there is the simpler one, which shares the same kitchen. Vegetarians will find good choices.

voyage.name: Gasthaus Ubl
voyage.content: The Austrian restaurant "Wirtshaus" serves traditional Viennese in authentic decor.

voyage.name: Kojiro Sushi-Bar
voyage.content: The first sushi bar in Vienna is a still-thriving crowded place. It is really small and easily missed. The green tea is free for customers.

voyage.name: Kojiro
voyage.content: The newer second branch of Kojiro is on a little square, where one can sit outside. It has a daily Japanese lunch menu and excellent sushi.

voyage.name: Nagoya Sushi
voyage.content: The Korean restaurant got modernised in 2013 and added Japanese food to its menu. It now sells fresh Sushi also for the go. They kept many Korean choices.

voyage.name: Tewa am Naschmarkt
voyage.content: Very bio place, popular with the early thirty-something bohemian locals.

voyage.name: Artner auf der Wieden
voyage.content: Belongs to a famous winery. Offers creative, fresh fare that tends to be on the lighter side than most Austrian cuisine. It has a 2 or 3-course business lunch menu offering, where one of the two options is vegetarian. Excellent wine cellar, reservations recommended.

voyage.name: Coté Sud
voyage.content: This small bistro cooks French cuisine with consistent good quality.

voyage.name: Otto e Mezzo
voyage.content: This restaurant, named after the Fellini film, is an Italian gem and offers a daily lunch menu. The Italian wines are well chosen and the pasta is lovely.

voyage.name: Schikaneder
voyage.content: The bar next to the cinema is popular with the mixed alternative crowd. Seats are usually only available if you go early.

voyage.name: Roxy Club
voyage.content: Operating since 1991 (with a short break only in 2012), this place stands out if you like stylish evenings with good music, including funk, soul, and hip hop. Look out for a small door to go downstairs.

voyage.name: Wieden Bräu
voyage.content: The brewery serves typical Austrian food. The beers are Märzen, Hell, Dunkel, Gemischtes and a monthly one.

voyage.name: Cafe Amacord
voyage.content: This café serves a lunch menu and international food choices including lots of vegetarian options. It has a nice laid back atmosphere, and is one of Vienna's rare non-smoking cafés. It has good Austrian whine and red wine choices.

voyage.name: Café Anzengruber
voyage.content: This place is packed for football games and serves mostly beer and wine. The Schnitzel is highly recommended by locals.

voyage.name: Heuer am Karlsplatz
voyage.content: This café is located very centrally on Karlsplatz, in the cube building of the Kunsthalle next to the University of Technology. It got relaunched in 2014 with stylish exterior and Thonet chairs inside. With good weather one can sit outside. Offers nice breakfasts too (eggs Florentine, French toast). They serve home-brewed Schlehen-Gin.

voyage.name: Radlager
voyage.content: The very stylish bike shop sells excellent coffee from an Italian espresso machine with Neapolitan roasted beans, juices, small sandwiches and salads.

voyage.name: Süssi
voyage.content: A French tea salon that sells excellent French patisserie (Macarons). Its interior is extravagant.

voyage.name: The breakfastclub
voyage.content: The place's specialty is good breakfasts, with many choices including vegetarian.

voyage.name: Café Wortner
voyage.content: A traditional Viennese café with a nice interior, but beware of the smoke and don't expect too much for the food. Wi-Fi access.

voyage.name: Vollpension
voyage.content: The original location of Vienna's intergenerational café, opened in 2015: senior citizens bake cakes to their own family recipes in a living-room-style interior. Breakfast served into the afternoon, outdoor seating, dogs welcome. Not wheelchair accessible. Reservations online.

voyage.name: AllYouNeed Hotel Vienna4***
voyage.content: The 3-star seasonal hotel is open from 1 July to 30 September and has 104 non-smoking rooms en-suite with hairdryer, flat-TV with satellite access and free internet, lift, lobby with seating, drinks and snacks machine, breakfast buffet, luggage storage, concierge service.

voyage.name: Hotel Erzherzog Rainer
voyage.alt: Schick Hotel Erzherzog Rainer in Vienna
voyage.content: The Hotel Erzherzog Rainer is one of the five Vienna Schick Hotels.

voyage.name: Das Triest Hotel
voyage.content: Designed by Sir Terence Conran, it has not only a special restaurant, but a special highly-rated bar too.

voyage.name: Margareten Platz
voyage.content: The biggest older square in Margareten.

voyage.name: Margareten-Hof
voyage.content: Built by the architects Ferdinand Fellner und Hermann Helmer in 1884/85.

voyage.name: Margaretenbrunnen
voyage.content: It was built to thank for the access to the fresh water pipeline going to the central imperial palace for Margareten in 1835/36. It features Saint Margarete killing a dragon.

voyage.name: Matzleinsdorfer Pfarrkirche
voyage.content: Two previous churches were located here, the most recent a Baroque building from the 18th century, which despite massive popular protest was demolished in 1965 due to traffic considerations. The new steel and concrete church was designed by the German architect Rudolf Schwarz and built between 1961-1965. A defining characteristic is the interplay of light concrete and dark glass, with the entry side featuring an over

voyage.name: The "Red Vienna": Community Housing of the 1920s and 1930s
voyage.content: During a short period from 1919 to 1933, the city of Vienna erected some 65,000 apartments of high quality for the impoverished working class. Highly noticeable is also the contemporary architecture of these buildings all across town, of which several interesting ones are clustered on a short stretch along Gürtel road. The style ranges from Art Déco to modernistic, the buildings have courtyards and often resemble for

voyage.name: Filmcasino
voyage.content: This very stylish cinema screens carefully chosen films.

voyage.name: Margaretenstraße
voyage.content: A chic shopping street with cozy cafes, galleries and up-market shops.

voyage.name: Fruth
voyage.content: The shop sells handmade chocolate.

voyage.name: On
voyage.content: A Chinese/Asian restaurant that gets consistent excellent gourmet reviews.

voyage.name: Rudi's Beisl
voyage.content: This Austrian Beisl likes to put "Panier" on everything.

voyage.name: Silberwirt
voyage.content: The "Beisl" is very popular amongst local Viennese.

voyage.name: Waldviertler Hof
voyage.content: This traditional Vienna restaurant offers good seasonal food and beer choices. The restaurant is non-smoking. Each room is specifically decorated, one of them is a traditional Zirben-Stube. The prices are fair and the portions big.

voyage.name: Weinschenke Franzensgasse
voyage.content: Chef Nikolai Kölbl serves enchanting versions of Viennese food. There are vegetarian options and the salads are good.

voyage.name: Woracziczky
voyage.content: A modern interpretation of traditional Viennese food like Tafelspitzsulz, Blunzentascherln, Zwiebelrostbraten, and Kalbsrahmgulasch. It is particularly popular for its casual atmosphere and tasty, delicate food.

voyage.name: Zum Schwarzen Adler
