voyage.content: The "Gasthaus" serves Viennese food and Hackl Bräu (workers' beer).

voyage.name: propeller
voyage.content: Cozy breakfast/lunch cafe with popular cocktails at night

voyage.name: Senhor Vinho
voyage.content: The Portuguese restaurant offers Bacalhao, Pastel de Nata and many different Portuguese wines.

voyage.name: Café Cuadro
voyage.content: The café serves breakfast, later cocktails and burgers, beware that people are heavily smoking.

voyage.name: Café Rüdigerhof
voyage.content: The Rüdigerhof is a typical Viennese café, hence expect rude waiters (treat them with humor) and have enough time to chill out. It offers nice seats outdoor under trees next to the Vienna river. Indoor can be very smoky.

voyage.name: Motto
voyage.content: It is a bar, a restaurant, a gallery and a concert location. The bar serves good wines and cocktails. It is a location for smokers.

voyage.name: Pub Klemo
voyage.content: The wine bar and shop has an incredible choice over 3000 different wines.

voyage.name: Reinprechtsstüberl
voyage.content: It serves upper Austrian monastery beer Schlägl and must ("Most").

voyage.name: Transporter Bar
voyage.content: The popular minimalistic bar with fair trade juices, long drinks features life DJ acts. It has free Wi-Fi access. The table-tennis table is used every Wednesday for a ping-pong evening.

voyage.name: WerkzeugH
voyage.content: The young architect Manfred Wuits together with the cook Zeljko Jovanovic transformed the previous tool hall/shop to an innovative popular bohemian bar. In summer time one can sit outside. There is free Wi-Fi. Usually on Sundays they organise special breakfast.

voyage.name: Hotel Allegro
voyage.content: Rough location on the corner of busy streets incluting Gürtel it is hence easy accessible and has fast connections.

voyage.name: The Art hotel Vienna
voyage.content: a modern 3-star hotel

voyage.name: Falkensteiner Hotel Wien Margareten
voyage.content: Opened in 2013 it is designed by architect Matteo Thun. It offers free Wi-Fi, a sauna, and a steam bath.

voyage.name: Pentahotel Vienna
voyage.content: The hotel has a café bar and stylish rooms designed by Matteo Thun.

voyage.name: Haydnhaus
voyage.price: €4 (adults), €3 (seniors/students/Vienna Card), free (children/youth under 19), free the first Sunday of every month
voyage.content: Joseph Haydn spent the final twelve years of his life in this home, during which time he composed the oratorios The Creation and The Seasons. The house has been a museum since 1899, and careful restoration has included the small garden, which is now also open to the public.

voyage.name: Haus des Meeres
voyage.content: A marvelous zoo, with a rain forest glasshouse, tiny apes, aquariums with sharks, and terrariums with reptiles and venomous snakes. Other highlights include an interesting exhibit of Mediterranean sea life and the aquarium's beloved sea turtle, "Puppi." The apes and birds are allowed to freely mingle with the visitors, but don't attempt to touch or feed them. It is in one of the surviving air raid defense towers from

voyage.name: Rahlstiege
voyage.content: The staircase connects the Mariahilfer and the Gumpendorfer Strasse. It was built in 1870.

voyage.name: Kletterzentrum Flakturm
voyage.hours: May-Sept: Mon Wed Fri-Sun 14:00-darkness; Tue Thu 12:00-darkness
voyage.content: On one side of the 2nd Worldwar bunker there are routes to climb high up until its roof with great views into the roofs of Vienna. The routes are usually hard and require some endurance. The alpine club organises courses for beginners and intermediate. On the other side there are boulder problems set. The outdoor climbing in middle of a historic city makes this a favorite choice for many climbers during the hot seaso

voyage.name: Theater an der Wien
voyage.content: This historic theater was founded by Emanuel Schikaneder (best known as Mozart's librettist for The Magic Flute). The building was designed by Franz Jäger, and completed in 1801. Since opening it has been the venue for many historic premieres of opera, theatre, and symphonies, including Beethoven's Fidelio in 1805 and Johann Strauss II's Die Fledermaus in 1874; since 2006 it has functioned mostly as an opera house. T

voyage.name: Raimund Theater
voyage.content: Constructed in 1893 as a venue for German folk dramas and plays, the building was later used for operettas. Since 1985 it has hosted German-language and international musicals.

voyage.name: Apollo Kino
voyage.content: A Cineplexx theater with plenty of choices including original versions. The cinema opened here in 1905. According to seat numbers it is one of the biggest in Vienna.

voyage.name: Haydn Kino
voyage.content: The theatre projects mostly English films in original version.

voyage.name: Topkino
voyage.content: During football championships they show the games in one of the cinema theatres. It is screening international artistic productions. For the bar see the drink section.

voyage.name: Naschmarkt
voyage.content: This is the largest of Vienna's 22 market places and provides a unique blend of typical Vienna costumely and oriental flair. Stroll through the market and be part of the amazing ambiance. If you like to cook, you will find all the spices you could possibly want at the Naschmarkt; on offer are regional and exotic fruits and vegetables, cheeses, meats, baked goods, and seafoods, as well as many small restaurants servin

voyage.name: Naschmarkt Flea Market
voyage.content: Need used lederhosen? How about a doner kebab at the Naschmarkt or an Austrian war bond from the first World War? This is the place to go on Saturdays. Pick through the detritus of an imperial society, you never know what you will find hidden under that stack of terrible fuzzy sweaters. Couture gowns, communist medals from all the former Eastern Bloc countries, tobacco pipes, broken pocket watches. Worth at least a f

voyage.name: Mariahilferstraße
voyage.content: The longest and most popular shopping avenue in Vienna, featuring all kinds of stores, many flagship stores from international brands, etc. More diverse and cosmopolitan than Kärntner Straße.

voyage.name: Polyklamott
voyage.content: Sells hand-picked second-hand clothes.

voyage.name: Ciclopia
voyage.content: This very fancy Viennese bike shop sells mostly Specialized mountain bikes or Italian road bikes. Their repair center is pricy, but very well known for their quality work. The shop is affiliated with a road racing team. From time to time they organise test rides for their customers.

voyage.name: Café Do An
voyage.content: Several salads are served. Free Wi-Fi. Usually it is well packed by a "bobo" public.

voyage.name: Eis-Greissler
voyage.content: Serves vegan and interesting ice-cream varieties.

voyage.name: Natsu I
voyage.content: Decent sushi.

voyage.name: Cafe Willendorf
voyage.content: The restaurant inside the lesbian and queer "Rosa Lilla Villa" serves good international food.

voyage.name: Disco Volante
voyage.content: Pizza with just enough and not too many toppings, and very Italian selection. Austrian ingredients, when used, are unusual specialties.

voyage.name: Kuishimbo
voyage.content: The smallest Japanese restaurant in town. All the dishes are homemade, and the owners claim that they pay attention to a proper balance of ingredients – being full can also be healthy. The place is so small that there is no toilet inside, you have to use the one in the Naschmarkt. The udon soups are excellent.

voyage.name: Mythos
voyage.content: A nice family-run Greek restaurant, with a good variety of items to choose from.

voyage.name: Naschmarkt Deli
voyage.content: Popular student meet place in Naschmarkt that sells directly sells good food with many vegetarian options directly from the Naschmarkt. The Italian café is recommended. Later in the evenings often a DJ plays.

voyage.name: Salzberg
voyage.content: The Salzberg restaurant serves Pongauer Kasnocken, made with special smoked cheese (Räucherkäse) from Salzburg province. There is a large selection of breakfast/brunch choices. The open air patio is on a quiet street.

voyage.name: Schwarze Katze
voyage.content: Georges Dimou, the singer, operates this traditional Greek restaurant.

voyage.name: Fischrestaurant Umar
voyage.content: Extremely good fish directly from their shop, which is the best and freshest seafood shop in Vienna. Wi-Fi is available. Changing daily lunch menu.

voyage.name: Neni
voyage.content: The best restaurant on the Naschmarkt with Isrealean carte.

voyage.name: Café Drechsler
voyage.content: The café is open during nights. It opened in 1919 by Engelbert Drechsler and is a traditional and popular all-night meeting point. It was carefully remodeled in 2007.

voyage.name: Cafe Jelinek
voyage.content: Small coffee place nicely lost in the middle of Mariahilf. In winter the rustic and warm oven is wonderful. In summer one can sit outdoors.

voyage.name: Cafe Restaurant Gschamster Diener
voyage.content: Smaller congenial Viennese café.

voyage.name: Café Ritter
voyage.content: A traditional Viennese cafe that is very popular due to its central location on Mariahilfer Strasse.

voyage.name: Café Savoy
voyage.content: The queer bar is centered around a big mirror and decorated in Makart style (Makartstil). Free WiFi. The café serves breakfast.

voyage.name: Café Sperl
voyage.content: A very traditional Viennese café, known to be frequented by contemporary Austrian writers including R. Menasse. It offers breakfast, cakes and a great atmosphere. Don't be put off by the Viennese brusqueness of the waiters – if possible counter with Viennese dialect and humor.

voyage.name: Phil
voyage.content: The bar/café sells also books, LPs and its furniture. The Pellini-Espresso is served from a Faema machine. Nice place to have breakfast.

voyage.name: Topkino
voyage.content: The bar of the cinema has good food too and serves wine and beer in a relaxed atmosphere. Unfortunately only up to 22:00 the bar is non-smoking, soon before people start smoking.

voyage.name: Barfly's Club
voyage.content: Big selection of fine and rare bottles.

voyage.name: Bar Italia
voyage.content: The Italian styled bar offers many different cocktails. Free Wi-Fi access. The music is primarily jazz and there is a dance floor.

voyage.name: futuregarden
voyage.content: Tiny little artsy bar, smoking permitted.

voyage.name: If dogs run free
voyage.content: The stylish and hip bar serves interesting cocktails.

voyage.name: Joanelli
voyage.content: The bar permits smoking and offers wines and vegan snacks.

voyage.name: Tanzcafé Jenseits
voyage.content: The bar serves good wine, with a popular dance floor (unusual in Vienna). Well-liked by women.

voyage.name: Red Carpet Hostel
voyage.content: Free WiFi, hostel bar, free welcome drink, shower/toilet in every room, backyard, free luggage storage. 1 Jul-14 Sep.

voyage.name: Hotel Kummer
voyage.content: Directly located on Mariahilferstraße.

voyage.name: Hotel Fuerst Metternich
voyage.content: The hotel is near Mariahilferstrasse and offers large breakfast. It hosts the Barfly's Club.

voyage.name: Das Tyrol
voyage.content: A small and comfortable hotel.

voyage.name: Leopold Museum
voyage.price: €12, students €8, children apprentice, disabled €7, €1 per person for the cloak room service
voyage.content: Has a strict policy of not allowing big bags inside the museum. Even your cameras (unless they can be tucked inside a small carry bag) will have to be deposited outside.

voyage.name: MUMOK
voyage.alt: Museum Moderner Kunst, Stiftung Ludwig Wien
voyage.content: Has a strict policy of not allowing big bags inside the museum. Even your cameras (unless they can be tucked inside a small carry bag) will have to be deposited outside. Has a self-service locker.

voyage.name: Kunsthalle Wien
voyage.content: Hosts highly-regarded exhibits of contemporary art, from Austrian and international artists.

voyage.name: WestLicht Center for Photography
voyage.content: Has a permanent exhibit of unusual cameras, including underwater and toy cameras, KGB spy cameras, and one of the 30 modified Hasselblad cameras used on the Apollo moon mission. The gallery hosts temporary exhibits, and the renowned "World Press Photo" show for the world's best press pictures.

voyage.name: Möbel Museum Wien
voyage.alt: Imperial Furniture Collection / Vienna Furniture Museum
voyage.content: Houses the largest furniture collection in the world. The exhibit displays furniture for all the Austrian emperors since Charles VI (the father of Maria Theresa), furniture by the Thonet Brothers, Jugendstil, and the Viennese Modernist movement. In addition, they show other contemporary Austrian architects and designers, such as E.A. Plischke, Margarete Schütte-Lihotzky, Luigi Blau, and Franz West. Besides the perman

voyage.name: Volkstheater Vienna
voyage.content: Designed by Hermann Helmer and Ferdinand Fellner, the theatre was built in 1889. With 970 seats it is the largest theatre in Vienna (larger than even the Burgtheater) and is one of the largest German-language theatres. It is located next to the Museumsquartier.

voyage.name: Theater Am Spittelberg
voyage.content: Historically one of the Pawlatschentheater, it has been renovated and is a venue for concerts and comedies.

voyage.name: Filmhaus am Spittelberg
voyage.content: With a single hall, this small and modern theatre screens documentary and arthouse films. Reservations are recommended.

voyage.name: Bellaria Kino
voyage.content: Charming and beautiful old-school cinema screening both old classic and original versions of contemporary films.

voyage.name: Museum Quarter
voyage.content: Has half a dozen small designer clothing shops.

voyage.name: Neubaugasse
voyage.content: The street has many innovative shops. A street market is held here twice a year.

voyage.name: Shu!
voyage.content: A collection of creative but still comfortable shoes from multiple brands, primarily Italian. Moderate prices.

voyage.name: Shu!Depot
voyage.content: A sales outlet of Shu!

voyage.name: Bergfuchs
voyage.content: The shop sells mountaineering equipment. You'll find climbing shoes, off-piste skis, all-weather clothing and other outdoor gear. The very knowledgeable salespeople offer great advice too, don't hesitate to ask. Various items are available through their online shop; keep an eye out for their special sales.

voyage.name: Bortolotti
voyage.address: Mariahilfer Straße 22 and 94 (the latter closed during winter!)
voyage.content: An ice cream parlour worth visiting. Ask particularly for the Campari-Orange ice cream or try some other exotic flavors.

voyage.name: Kolar Zieglergassemore
voyage.content: Nice pubs/beisls. They have a tasty Fladenbrot as well as their own beer.

voyage.name: Maschu
voyage.content: A trendy hang out place with its own unique vibe, in the area of the city frequented by art students. It is famous for its falafel.

voyage.name: Natsu II
voyage.content: Serves decent sushi.

voyage.name: Schnitzelwirt Schmidt
voyage.content: The traditional Viennese food is excellent and served in truly prodigious portions. The Bauernschmaus (Farmer's Feast), a nearly incapacitatingly large schnitzel plate, which in combination with any of the wonderful on-tap beers, may necessitate an afternoon nap.

voyage.name: Amerlingbeisl
voyage.content: The restaurant has a good selection of food with vegetarian options too. Inside smoking is permitted, but this is not so much of a problem for non-smokers in summer when it's possible to sit outside. The bar serves beer, some wines, and standard cocktails.

voyage.name: Bombay
voyage.content: It serves the best Bombay Gin in Vienna. Among Indian restaurants in Vienna it is an institution, offering good food and large servings for reasonable prices.

voyage.name: DschungelCafe
voyage.content: A very child-friendly cafe and restaurant, located in the same building as the DschungelWien.at children's theater.

voyage.name: Gasthaus Grünauer
voyage.content: A Viennese restaurant serving high-quality food with a good selection of wines.

voyage.name: MQdaily
voyage.content: Located next to the entry of the MQ, this place is quite small and packed.

voyage.name: I Ragazzi
voyage.content: This Italian restaurant has good pizzas and pastas for good prices. Their fish soup is highly recommended. Outdoor seating is available in the summer.

voyage.name: I Terroni
voyage.content: Same crew as I Ragazzi but less crowded. The restaurant serves good Italian pizzas and pastas.

voyage.name: Tian Bistro am Spittelberg
voyage.hours: Tue 17:00-23:00, Wed-Fri 11:00-23:00, Sat Sun and holidays 09:00-23:00; kitchen open until 1 hr before closing
voyage.content: Operated by star chef Paul Ivić of TIAN Restaurant, the bistro serves more affordable meals than at his main restaurant, all of them vegetarian with many vegan options. Reservations can be made online.

voyage.name: Le Troquet
voyage.content: A popular French bistro in a shabby chic setting. They play jazz and serve good wines; smoking permitted.

voyage.name: Ulrich
voyage.content: In a calm paved passage the small restaurant (Beisl) serves a breakfast and has a lunch menu.

voyage.name: LUX Restaurant
voyage.content: One part of the establishment is a café, and the other a bar and restaurant (by the Spittelberggase entrance). The food is regional and exquisite. Free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Veganista
voyage.content: Operated by two vegan sisters, this is the first vegan ice cream shop in Vienna. It has become so popular that they have now expanded with four more branches in the Vienna area. Flavours change by season, many of them exotic.

voyage.name: Blue Box
voyage.content: This longstanding bar was legendary during the 1980s and 90s. It serves breakfast with many vegetarian options, as well as special beer from Vorarlberg.

voyage.name: Café Leopold
voyage.content: A classy modern café that becomes a bar in the evening. There may be a cover charge for the evening parties downstairs.

voyage.name: Cafe Nil
voyage.content: This Middle Eastern cafe is modeled after old coffee houses in Cairo and Alexandria, and serves many organic foods. Takeaway is available, although the atmosphere really invites one to linger.

voyage.name: Café Westend
voyage.content: Opened in 1900, the café has historic decor with old tables and mirrors. It is situated in front of the main railway station Westbahnhof, which makes it practical to wait here for upcoming trains.

voyage.name: Das Möbel
voyage.content: Hip café. Take a close look at the tables, chairs, and lamps – every piece of furniture is unique and for sale.

voyage.name: Espresso
voyage.content: Very cool little 1950s-style café with good tunes, attracting an eclectic crowd. Owned by the nearby Wirr bar.

voyage.name: Europa
voyage.content: The café is often bursting at the seams, but good tunes and decent service prevail. Good people watching and decor. One of Vienna's most popular meeting points. The bar serves warm food til late hours.

voyage.name: TartaTata
voyage.content: This small café serves French croissants, pains au chocolat, and tartes.

voyage.name: Rote Bar
voyage.content: Lovely interior to savour a relaxed drink inside the Volkstheater. From time to time it serves as a small venue for excellent concerts. The door is on the left side of the main entrance for the Volkstheater.

voyage.name: Siebensternbräu
voyage.content: An excellent Biergarten. They serve their own brews, which are all excellent. There is the usual assortment of bar food, friendly staff, and outdoor seating underneath an old linden tree in the middle of a hidden courtyard. Everyday from 11:00-16:00 a selection of hearty dishes is served for €5-6. Move indoors well before 23:00, because a local noise ordinance requires the bar to shut down the patio and the interior

voyage.name: Youth Hostel Vienna-Myrthengasse
voyage.content: Institutional.

voyage.name: K+K Maria Theresia
voyage.price: Regular doubles around €125 through frequently available special offers, €145+ as rack rates
voyage.content: Offers a gourmet breakfast buffet. Overall, this is a good choice both for a business traveler and for a family with a toddler; comfortable for non-smokers. Heated floors in bathroom. Rooms are modern and each has a full tea set, wired internet in every room, electronic safe box, hairdrier, minibar. Small sauna adjoining a tiny gym open until at least 23:00. Breakfast from 06:30. On the downside, few steps to overcom

voyage.name: Falkensteiner Hotel am Schottenfeld
voyage.content: The hotel's contemporary design is a refreshing departure from the usually stodgy appearance of most Viennesse hotels. Be mindful when booking a suite – some of them come with steeply sloping roofs.

voyage.name: Arcotel Wimberger Wien
voyage.content: A surprisingly ordinary hotel from a chain priding itself in adding a designer touch to its properties. What matters, however, is that the (quite awfully decorated) rooms close to the Westbahnhof can be had for a reasonable price, and the service level is good for Vienna.

voyage.name: InterCityHotel Wien
voyage.content: The InterCityHotel chain, a part of the German Steigenberger Group, focuses on hotels right next to train stations. This particular one is a block away from Westbahnhof, but still offers all the usual amenities, including a free all-day ticket for public transit. The decor is simple but modern and tasteful, especially for Viennesse standards. Some more expensive Business Plus rooms feature terraces with a view over t

voyage.name: NH Wien City
voyage.content: NH brings the peace of mind by offering predictability of the chain's usual standards. Of note is the generous size of rooms (25m²), unusual for Vienna, as well as the fact that all of them are equipped with a kitchenette.

voyage.name: NH Collection Wien Zentrum
voyage.content: If the large rooms of the NH Wien City are still not enough for you, the chain's other property down the road offers suites of 35-50m² at similar prices.

voyage.name: 25hours Hotel beim MuseumsQuartier
voyage.content: The Viennese foothold of the outlandish designer hotel chain spanning the German-speaking countries, with a rooftop terrace bar so popular that even staying guests may find it hard to get in. The location between university campuses and the Museumsquartier helps enhance the artsy/cultural/intellectual setting.

voyage.name: Hotel Sans Souci
voyage.content: Opened in December 2012, Hotel Sans Souci Wien is right across from the Museum Quarter and a 5-minute walk from the Ringstraße. The large spa area includes an indoor pool. Free Wi-Fi is available.

voyage.name: Palais Auersperg
voyage.content: The palace was built in the early 18th century, and expanded in the late 18th century under the ownership of Prince Adam von Auersperg. Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach drew up the first plans; later designs are attributed to Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt. In 1945 the Austrian resistance group O5 (meaning OE = Oesterreich) met here. Historically it has always been a center for music, hosting many celebrations and ba

voyage.name: Palais Damian
voyage.content: The palace changed hands frequently, with each owner making their own adaptations to the building. The central sections date from the early 18th century, while the second floor was a later addition.

voyage.name: Palais Schönborn
voyage.content: This impressive Baroque palace was built in 1706-1711 following the designs of Johann Lukas von Hildebrandt. It houses the Museum of Folk Life and Folk Art (Museum für Volkskunde) (see listing below).

voyage.name: Palais Strozzi
voyage.content: The palace was built in 1702, and once had a garden that extended to Pfeilgasse. Renovations in 1996 led to the rediscovery of old paintings dating to the period of the building's construction.

voyage.name: Piarist Church
voyage.content: The Baroque church Maria Treu was probably designed by Lukas von Hildebrandt. The church has eight chapels and is decorated with frescoes made by Franz Anton Maulbertsch. It is considered as an important religious building of its time. In 1949 it was elevated to Basilica minor.

voyage.name: Wiener Schuhmuseum
voyage.hours: Every second Tue of the month, 16:00-19:00
voyage.content: The only museum of its kind in Austria, with displays focusing on the history of shoemaking.

voyage.name: Österreichisches Museum für Volkskunde
voyage.alt: The Austrian Museum of Folk Life and Folk Art
voyage.content: Founded in 1895 and housed in the Schönborn Garden Palace, this museum is dedicated to preserving the traditional folk art of Austria and of central Europe, with rotating exhibits as well as a permanent display. There is a museum library and gift shop onsite, and guided tours are available in German, English, and Slovak.

voyage.name: Kletterzentrum ÖGV
voyage.hours: Sep-Jun: Mon-Fri 10:00-23:00, Sat Sun holidays 14:00-20:00; Jul Aug: Mon-Fri 10:00-17:00
voyage.content: A small climbing gym inside Vienna has walls in an indoor court, in the cellar, and more upstairs. The gym offers courses for various ages and climbing experience, with highly-motivated trainers and climbers. The boulders are known to be very demanding on endurance, and there are some special circuits set up upstairs. Every autumn they organise a friendly boulder competition.

voyage.name: Theater in der Josefstadt
voyage.content: Opened in 1776, this is the oldest continually-operating theater in Vienna. At its reopening following a remodeling in 1822 Beethoven directed his commissioned piece Die Weihe des Hauses (The Consecration of the House). Since 1858, it has focused exclusively on theater, and music is no longer performed here. Famous cast members have included Johann Nestroy, Otto Schenk, and Klaus Maria Brandenauer.

voyage.name: Vienna's English Theatre
voyage.hours: On performance days: Mon-Fri 10:00-19:00, Sat and holidays 17:00-19:00; non-performance days: Mon-Fri 10:00-17:00
voyage.content: The oldest English-language theatre in continental Europe. Tickets can be purchased online.

voyage.name: Essenswert
voyage.content: The seasonal products are to be ordered online until Tuesday morning and can be picked up on Fridays. The shop sells special bread, vegetables, cheese and wines.

voyage.name: muso koroni
voyage.content: Vegan clothing and accessories.

voyage.name: Potstill
voyage.content: The shop offers a huge selection (1000 different single malts), with good advice on choosing whisky. It also offers interesting or not so common whiskey-chocolate combinations.

voyage.name: Vinoe - Die Niederösterreich-vinothek
voyage.content: The shop sells a variety fine wines from Lower Austria, including from the regions of Wachau, Langenlois, and Retz. They really know their selection – don't hesitate to ask for recommendations.

voyage.name: Tunnel
voyage.content: Student's place. Nice breakfast, live music every day starting about 21:00.

voyage.name: Puerta del Sol
voyage.content: One of the best tapas bars in Vienna. Both the cold and warm tapas are excellent, and one can choose from amongst 90 wines.

voyage.name: Curry Insel
voyage.content: Sri Lankan restaurant with a good range of vegetarian dishes. Free WiFi.

voyage.name: Deli Bluem
voyage.content: The vegan restaurant cooks local ingredients.

voyage.name: Il Sestante
voyage.content: This Italian restaurant serves pizza fired in a stone oven. It has a nice view of the Maria Treu plaza, with outdoor seating in the summer.

voyage.name: Konoba
voyage.content: The delicious aromas of garlic and grilled fish invite the passerby into this Croatian seafood restaurant.

voyage.name: Prinz Ferdinand
voyage.content: An Austrian Beisl that serves good food and even some vegetarian options.

voyage.name: Schnattl
voyage.content: For more than 25 years the restaurant has been serving Viennese and international cuisine of a high standard.

voyage.name: Speisekammer
voyage.content: A small new fancy underground restaurant, with a rotating roster of young chefs who prepare freely-improvised dishes. A special feature is the surprise menu (Überraschungsmenu), where you can choose the ingredients of your meal, but not the manner of preparation.

voyage.name: Cafe der Provinz
voyage.content: Cute little coffee place sells mostly organic products. Serves breakfast, gallettes, and crêpes.

voyage.name: Café Eiles
voyage.content: This café has been operating since 1840, when the building was completed. The interior dates from the last redesign in 1933.

voyage.name: Café Florianihof
voyage.content: A very popular café that has been redecorated. It serves good food with many vegetarian options for fair prices and typical Austrian desserts like "Topfen-knöderl" or "Powiderl-Tascherl". Free Wi-Fi. Most of the places are non-smoking.

voyage.name: Café Merkur
voyage.content: On Saturdays and Sundays offers breakfast almost all day. Due to its good prices it is a popular hang-out for students. Has Wi-Fi access.

voyage.name: Kaffeemodul
voyage.content: A tiny coffee gem in Vienna, easily overlooked by passersby, with very skilled baristas.

voyage.name: People on Caffeine
voyage.content: Hidden away in a former Catholic sacristy, this café offers fair trade and special roasted coffee. Serves espresso and many of the newer filtered coffee styles.

voyage.name: Gürtel
voyage.content: Many bars and music-oriented venues are under the elevated subway tracks.

voyage.name: B72
voyage.content: The bar also serves as a venue for hip hop and modern music concerts.

voyage.name: Chelsea
voyage.content: Serving a wide range of international beers, this popular place is often fully-packed.

voyage.name: Rhiz
voyage.content: Rhiz promotes experimental music for an alternative audience; it's well worth checking out the online program of upcoming concerts. This bar tends to be particularly smoky.

voyage.name: Hotel Graf Stadion
voyage.content: The house was built in the Biedermeier Epoche style in 1824/1825 and is registered as a historic monument; it has been run as a hotel since 1897. 39 singles and doubles with bath with shower/WC, hair dryer, clothesline, SAT-Flatscreen-TV, radio, telephone and free WLAN in the entire hotel.

voyage.name: Mercure Josefshof Vienna
voyage.content: The hotel is located on a quiet side street. It provides free Wi-Fi and has a small basement garage for cars.

voyage.name: The Levante Laudon
voyage.content: Rents apartments on a quiet street behind the city hall (Rathaus). All apartments have a usable small kitchen; the two-room apartments have separated living rooms and bedrooms. Perfectly suitable for families.

voyage.name: Hotel Zipser
voyage.content: The Jugendstil hotel in the centre of Vienna is a family-run business, and offers special rates for families.

voyage.name: The Levante Parliament
voyage.content: The centrally-located boutique hotel has a beautiful atrium and the Nemtoi Restaurant-Bar. Has free Wi-Fi, as well as fitness and spa rooms.
